title: Odessa's Grocery and adopting Michael
summary: Odessa saved enough to buy a grocery, now a self-service market, and they adopted a son, Michael, around 1955.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When I come back, this girl has saved all that money and had a grocery.
I talked to her. She got a grocery in Chicago called Odessa's Grocery. A guy was going out of business and I think she got it from him for $1,200.

And she got her a little grocery store and called it Odessa's Grocery, and she saved her money, because, you know, she could save a dollar. Oh, she could save a dollar. If Odessa was going to save money, she'd hide it and she'd put it away. Now, at times I had seen money that she had hid and I'd say, "Odessa," I said, "what is this? What's this money here?" She said that don't belong to me. Immediately she'd put it away. She doesn't have it anymore.
And so later on the next thing I know she -- today she has a self-service market, you know. And we
-- and she calls it Michael's Grocery
And you adopted a kid. When was that?
That's right. 195 -- about 1957. Michael was 19 this past March 1956. So 1955, just about, we adopted Michael.
And put him through school. He was going to a Presbyterian school, I think.
